patterns.name: Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA
patterns.summary: Every hour, around the clock, the trader on shift at the Portland real-time desk calls the service-customer generator (Frontier, and until it moves to BPA's automatic system, Grays Harbor) for its actual output, then calls BPA to read the actual figure in, then initials the hour on the services sheet. patterns.name: Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets

In March 2001 Bryce Baxter set up a four-ticket accounting treatment that has to be redone by hand every month before flash. Someone zeroes the price on that month's HPL sale to GLO. Julie Meyers did this for January and February 2001, but the March deal was copied from January's with the price still on it, and March onward was never completed. patterns.name: Overriding MIPS zero volumes in POPS by hand
patterns.summary: For outside-measured and mirrored (bidirectional) meters, measurement's system (MIPS) gets no volume until month-end, so its nightly file sends POPS a zero. That zero becomes the best available volume (BAV) and replaces the estimate Gas Control sends. POPS then passes the zero to Sitara, so purchase expense drops out of the desk's P&L and sits in the UA4 account. Pipeline Operations schedulers have to spot these zeros, get Gas Control's volumes and override POPS, then re-allocate the meter. A later nightly roll can write the zero back over a corrected meter, as happened at Valero Texoma on 3/21/2000. When a zero is missed, it takes an escalation by email: on 3/21/2000 Lauri Allen, Charlotte Hawkins, Michael Eiben and Gary Anderson wrote about it, and on 4/4/2000 Robert Lloyd had to ask again for Enron Methanol because his first note was not read as a request. patterns.name: Chasing origination recognized on a book's P&L that does not match what was granted
patterns.summary: When a trading book grants origination to an originator group (for example FT-Central to IM-Central / Middle Market), the grant goes on the origination schedule and the receiving book records the origination on its own P&L as a separate step. Each evening an analyst in the P&L group (Gabriel Monroy, Binh Pham, Rahmaan Mwongozi) compares what each book recognized with the schedule.
